“If you want to keep a secret, you must also hide it from yourself.”
_— George Orwell, __1984_



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e617ab51-fd48-407f-a30c-9c4713fe789b/unnamed.jpg?t=1793743779)
Caption: 

# Private keys as easy as 1,2,3

The basic idea of elliptic-curve cryptography is that it's easy to go forward along a mathematically defined curve and effectively impossible to go back. 

What you move forward toward is a public key: a two-dimensional point (x,y) located somewhere along a “curve” defined by a mathematical equation.

(I used scare quotes there because the equation produces a scatterplot of coordinates that only a mathematician could identify as a curve.) 

What gets you there is a private key: Starting from a fixed base point on the curve (G), you add G to itself some number of times (d) to arrive at the public key (x,y).

D is the private key: an integer you plug into the curve’s equation to get to the public key.

The practical result is that deriving a public key from a private key (going forward) takes milliseconds, but deriving a private key from a public key (going backward) would take billions of years. 

I can’t explain exactly why going backward takes as long as that, but I know it has something to do with elliptic curve math.

The important thing is what this makes possible: e-commerce, private messaging, biometric authentication, cryptocurrency.

Elliptic-key cryptography allows two complete strangers to communicate securely over a public network without having agreed on a secret code in advance.

To participate, all you need is a private key that’s long enough that no one will guess it.

Because someone might try.

In crypto, for example, private keys typically look something like: 4f9a2c88e5d1b703e498c116a82705f32b859e4d07c31fae81b6dc24089e9247. 

Despite the letters involved, this is just a number. Each hexadecimal digit in the string (number or letter) represents four bits of binary data (f = 1111, 8 = 1000, e

81909.subject: Tokenization Briefing: BNB Chain Flips Ethereum?
81909.body:
----------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b35d8526-fea4-4141-81d2-c5bf58b65a37/unnamed__23_.png?t=1789408235)
Follow image link: (https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/tokenization-briefing)
Caption: 


--------------------
GM. Wall Street spent the week deciding how it wants tokenization to work. DTCC launched its tokenization service, NYSE signed four more transfer agents and put Broadridge in charge of onchain shareholder voting, 50 public companies objected to having their shares listed on OKXICE, and the CFTC cleared the first perpetual futures on US stocks for regulated exchanges.

In today’s issue, we cover the latest developments in tokenization on Wall Street, how tokenization-focused stocks have been performing now that the infrastructure is continuing its momentum, and how tokenized ETFs are increasing in value.

Thanks for subscribing!


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2b004db0-6294-4fd0-8714-d02ab4c3e317/TB9_Stat_Strip.png?t=1793741819)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
# ==Top of Mind==

## _Wall Street’s Tokenization Model Takes Shape_

DTCC’s Tokenization Service went live on October 28. There are 20 DTC participants including JPMorgan, Citi, Morgan Stanley, Fidelity and Bank of America, with more firms onboarding on a rolling basis. The service launched on Canton and DTCC’s own private chain, with additional chains planned for 2027.

NYSE and ICE are also making progress towards building out a tokenized trading platform. Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate joined Securitize and tZERO as transfer agents. The three traditional agents serve nearly 5,000 listed companies, almost 99% of the S&P 500. Broadridge will also run proxy voting onchain so investors can vote from a wallet, a broker app or ProxyVote.

The same week, issuer objections to OKXICE, the OKX and ICE venue that would tokenize US stocks without issuer involvement, reached 50 in its October 30 notice, up from nine on October 15. Nvidia, Costco and Nike were among the latest.


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fcd07e7b-a679-426c-80f1-fe0dba8bb021/TB9_OKXICE_Issuer_Objections_v2.png?t=1793742221)
Caption: 

----------
On Monday the CFTC approved the first perpetual futures on individual US stocks for registered exchanges, a product that until now existed only offshore, days after ICE said it would bring Hyperliquid’s perpetuals to US users.

81906.subject: Hackers stole $6.3b from Binance. We’re tracking exchange flows
81906.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5fe102f5-8ba2-4584-a1ba-0109facdf9c3/Top_banner_Flare_report.jpg?t=1793724752)
Follow image link: (https://defillama.com/research/report/how-flare-uses-data-to-expand-what-capital-can-do)
Caption: 

In the span of about 20 minutes, hackers stole $6.3b from Binance’s hot wallets on Friday, resulting in the largest crypto hack on record.

Binance froze withdrawals for roughly 45 hours. Stablecoin issuers froze $3b of USDT & USDC.

Track Live Binance Reserves (https://defillama.com/exchange/binance?section=reserves&includeOwnTokens=true)

Since withdrawals resumed, users have withdrawn over $6.4b. 7d Net inflows for the world’s largest crypto exchange currently sit at -$12b.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/961bc03b-856f-4581-ada3-2a23cfce4bab/image.png?t=1793719794)
Follow image link: (https://defillama.com/exchange/binance?section=reserves&includeOwnTokens=true)
Caption: 

The attackers gained access through a compromised employee computer.

An exploiter’s wallet supplied $60m USDT on Aave and borrowed $44m of WETH, leading to a temporary freeze of Aave’s v3 & v4 lending markets. Markets were unfrozen shortly after.

Stablecoin market cap [fell to its lowest level](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) since October 2025, but there’s currently no sign of stablecoin or lending stress. Other major exchanges have seen [net inflows](https://defillama.com/cexs) over the last 7 days.

After two days of net outflows following the hack, Binance saw nearly $3b in inflows today.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e0b46f99-b472-4af7-91e4-ebb0e00d6d7e/binance-inflows-by-token_2026-11-03__2_.png?t=1793718372)
Follow image link: (https://defillama.com/exchange/binance?section=reserves&includeOwnTokens=true)
Caption: 

These outflows were about 8% of Binance’s reserves at their peak: relatively manageable compared to Bybit’s hack in February 2025 that was 36% of reserves. Binance used about half of its $1b SAFU fund and corporate funds to cover the losses. 

Read [Binance’s response update here](https://x.com/binance/status/2117626126214504729?a=q_HDvHN-hGVLRXynk6k&s=20).

Stablecoins make up over 65% of the $6.3b in net outflows from [Binance’s tracked wallets](https://defillama.com/exchange/binance?includeOwnTokens=true&section=reserves) since withdrawals resumed. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/68c2703d-e100-4f8a-a3ef-4a0697c22b80/binance-tracked-wallet-net-outflow-by-asset-nov-1-to-nov-3-14-00-utc-snapshot_2026-11-03.png?t=1793720073)
